title: A JFrog API key value with no header or password position around it
summary: A synthetic value alone in prose with no header name, no password position and no recognisable prefix.
rationale: JFrog's pages state two forms that they do not reconcile: the reference page's pattern of the four characters AKCp followed by 69 alphanumerics (73 in all, deprecated from Artifactory 7.47.x), and the create-API-key reference example of 44 characters with base64 punctuation and no AKCp prefix, unchanged since 2025-09-06. Which form belongs to which release, and whether the example is schematic, are not stated, and the end of authentication is not stated either (End of Life is announced, new-key creation is blocked from 7.98 and blocking use of an existing key is an administrator setting that is off by default). No bare-value fixture is built to either shape, because a shape-based expectation would choose between the two forms; the planned fixtures, if a JFrog statement ever settles it, are one value of each documented form in prose. The header and password-position Case does not depend on any of this.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for a bare value: the two JFrog statements of the key form conflict (claim two-provider-statements-of-form-unreconciled, open question api-key-format-conflict) and no carrier is present. A JFrog per-release format statement or a statement that the example is schematic would settle it.

sources.supports: API Keys follow this pattern: .*\bAKCp[A-Za-z0-9]{69}\b.*, starting with AKCp and including 69 alphanumeric characters.
sources.locator: Comparing Identity Reference Tokens With API Keys

sources.supports: The create-API-key reference example is 44 characters with base64 punctuation and no AKCp prefix; the page states it as an example only.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
